scenes.section_title:
* Primary learning objective: Formulate the tangential equation of motion \\(\sum F_t = m a_t\\), proving that the net tangential force component acts exclusively to change speed magnitude (\\(a_t = \dot{v} = dv/dt = v\, dv/ds\\)), directed along the instantaneous path tangent \\(\mathbf{u}_t\\).
* Essential and supporting perspectives: Essential: Path-Tangential Force Action Perspective (correlating net force parallel to motion directly with scalar speed rate change), Speed Differential Energy Perspective (\\(\sum F_t\, ds = m v\, dv\\)). Supporting: Friction-Propulsion Balance Perspective.
* Important evidence gaps: Normal directional turning forces and binormal lateral forces are treated in separate orthogonal equations.
scenes.generated_prompt:
Scene Type: Process
Learning Target: Formulate tangential equation of motion $\sum F_t = m a_t$, proving that net tangential force component acts exclusively to change speed magnitude (\\(a_t = \dot{v} = dv/dt\\)).
Scene Objects and Initial State: 2D coordinate viewport featuring race car $C$ (red vehicle model, mass $m = 1000.0\text{ kg}$) traveling along curved track. Moving $n$-$t$ coordinate frame attached to car $C$: Tangential axis $t$ along velocity direction $\mathbf{u}_t$, Normal axis $n$ pointing inward toward curvature center $O'$. Vector overlay attached to car $C$: Blue net tangential force arrow $\sum F_t$ pointing forward along $t$-axis, Red tangential acceleration vector arrow $a_t$ parallel to $\sum F_t$. Digital readout panel: engine drive force $F_{drive} = 3600.0\text{ N}$, aerodynamic drag $F_{drag} = 1000.0\text{ N}$, net tangential force $\sum F_t = 2600.0\text{ N}$, tangential acceleration $a_t = 2.6\text{ m/s}^2$, car speed $v(t)$, live formula $\sum F_t = m a_t$.
Time Behavior: Continuous time execution updates car speed $v(t) = v_0 + \int a_t\, dt$, while adjusting drive or brake force sliders dynamically resizes red tangential acceleration vector arrow $a_t$.
Custom Perspectives: Pure Magnitude Rate Perspective: Demonstrating visually that net tangential force $\sum F_t$ acts exclusively along path tangent $\mathbf{u}_t$ to alter speed magnitude $v$, leaving trajectory curvature bending entirely to normal forces.
Governing Rules: Tangential equation of motion: $\sum F_t = m a_t$. Tangential acceleration definitions: $a_t = \frac{dv}{dt} = \dot{v} = v \frac{dv}{ds}$. Work-energy integration relation: $\int \sum F_t\, ds = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 - \frac{1}{2}m v_0^2$.
Learner Investigations and Controls:
- Engine Drive Force Slider (\\(F_{drive}\\)): Learner adjusts forward thrust force $F_{drive} \in [0.0\text{ N}, 6000.0\text{ N}]$.
- Brake Retarding Force Slider (\\(F_{brake}\\)): Learner adjusts braking resistance $F_{brake} \in [0.0\text{ N}, 8000.0\text{ N}]$.
- Aerodynamic Drag Toggle: Enables or disables speed-dependent drag resistance $F_{drag} = c v^2$.
- Formula Calculation Panel Toggle: Shows or hides scalar force summation breakdown (\\(\sum F_t = F_{drive} - F_{drag} - F_{brake} = m a_t\\)).
- Investigation Action: Set $F_{drive} = 3600.0\text{ N}, F_{drag} = 1000.0\text{ N}$ and observe forward acceleration, then apply brake slider $F_{brake} = 5000.0\text{ N}$.
- Visible Consequence: At initial state, net force calculates as $\sum F_t = 3600 - 1000 = 2600.0\text{ N}$; red acceleration vector arrow points forward along $t$-axis with magnitude $a_t = 2.6\text{ m/s}^2$; speed meter $v(t)$ increases steadily. Applying brakes updates net force to $\sum F_t = 3600 - 1000 - 5000 = -2400.0\text{ N}$; red acceleration arrow flips $180^\circ$ backward along negative $t$-axis with magnitude $a_t = -2.4\text{ m/s}^2$; car speed meter $v(t)$ decelerates rapidly toward rest.
Linked Representations: Race car position on curved track, blue $\sum F_t$ arrow length, red $a_t$ arrow orientation, digital speed meter $v(t)$, and scalar equation readout panel are fully synchronized.
Visual Outcome and Misconception Contrast: Proves that tangential force component controls speed magnitude rate change (\\(a_t = \dot{v}\\)), correcting the misconception that tangential force causes directional turning on curved tracks.
Acceptance Requirements:
1. Verify $a_t = 2.6\text{ m/s}^2$ for $m = 1000.0\text{ kg}, \sum F_t = 2600.0\text{ N}$.
2. Verify $a_t = 2.0\text{ m/s}^2$ for $m = 1200.0\text{ kg}, \sum F_t = 2400.0\text{ N}$.
3. Verify red acceleration arrow flips direction when net tangential force becomes negative.
Limitations: Normal directional forces and binormal forces are omitted.

* Primary learning objective: Formulate the tangential equation of motion \\(\sum F_t = m a_t\\), proving that the net tangential force component acts exclusively to change speed magnitude (\\(a_t = \dot{v} = dv/dt = v\, dv/ds\\)), directed along the instantaneous path tangent \\(\mathbf{u}_t\\).
* Essential and supporting perspectives: Essential: Path-Tangential Force Action Perspective (correlating net force parallel to motion directly with scalar speed rate change), Speed Differential Energy Perspective (\\(\sum F_t\, ds = m v\, dv\\)). Supporting: Friction-Propulsion Balance Perspective.

first_output.core_understanding:
* Baseline concept: When a particle moves along a curved path, Newton's Second Law \\(\sum \mathbf{F} = m\mathbf{a}\\) resolved along the tangential axis \\(t\\) yields \\(\sum F_t = m a_t\\). Tangential acceleration \\(a_t = \dot{v} = \frac{dv}{dt} = v \frac{dv}{ds}\\) represents the time rate of change of speed. If \\(\sum F_t > 0\\) (in direction of motion \\(\mathbf{u}_t\\)), the particle accelerates (speeds up). If \\(\sum F_t < 0\\) (opposite to motion), the particle decelerates (slows down). If \\(\sum F_t = 0\\), speed remains constant (\\(a_t = 0\\)).
* Time Perspective: Application of tangential force over time accumulates speed according to \\(v(t) = v_0 + \int a_t\, dt\\).
* Custom perspectives: Pure Magnitude Rate Perspective: Tangential force alters only how fast the particle moves, leaving trajectory curvature bending entirely to normal forces.
* Perspective connections: Integrating tangential force over displacement \\(s\\) yields work-energy relations (\\(\int \sum F_t\, ds = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 - \frac{1}{2}m v_0^2\\)).

* Literal vs. metaphorical: Race car, track curve, force arrows, and acceleration vector arrow are literal physical vector overlays.

first_output.conceptual_summary: * The tangential equation of motion \\(\sum F_t = m a_t\\) relates net tangential forces along path tangent \\(\mathbf{u}_t\\) directly to rate of speed change (\\(a_t = \dot{v}\\)). first_output.colloquial_egyptian_explanation: * معادلة الحركة في الاتجاه المماسي \\(\sum F_t = m a_t\\) بسيطة جداً: القوة المماسية الصافية المؤثرة على الجسم في اتجاه حركته هي المسئولة الوحيدة عن تغيير مقدار السرعة (تسارع أو تباطؤ). لو المحرك بيدي قوة للأمام أكبر من المقاومة، الجسم هيركب عجلة مماسية موجبة \\(a_t = \dot{v}\\) وسرعته هتزيد. ولو دوست فرامل، القوة المماسية هتبقى لورا وسرعته هتقل.
first_output.laws_if_any:
* Tangential equation of motion: \\(\sum F_t = m a_t\\)
* Tangential acceleration relations: \\(a_t = \frac{dv}{dt} = \dot{v} = v \frac{dv}{ds}\\)
* Speed differential work relation: \\(\int \sum F_t\, ds = \int m v\, dv = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 - \frac{1}{2}m v_0^2\\)
* Units: Force in Newtons (\\(\text{N}\\)), Mass in \\(\text{kg}\\), Acceleration in \\(\text{m/s}^2\\).
first_output.real_life_example:

scenes.section_title:
* Primary learning objective: Formulate the normal equation of motion \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\), establishing that centripetal force \\(\sum F_n\\) acts perpendicular to motion toward the center of curvature \\(O'\\), causing direction change proportional to \\(v^2\\) and inversely proportional to \\(\rho\\).
* Essential and supporting perspectives: Essential: Center-Directed Centripetal Force Perspective (identifying \\(\sum F_n\\) as the required inward physical force pulling particle into a curved trajectory), Curvature Geometry Reaction Perspective (linking \\(a_n = v^2/\rho\\) to curvature radius \\(\rho\\)). Supporting: Friction Lateral Grip Limit Perspective (\\(F_n \le \mu_s N\\)).
* Important evidence gaps: Outward centrifugal force is a non-inertial fictitious frame effect and is excluded in inertial frame kinetics.
scenes.generated_prompt:
Scene Type: Process
Learning Target: Formulate normal equation of motion $\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}$, establishing that centripetal force $\sum F_n$ acts toward curvature center $O'$, causing direction change proportional to $v^2/\rho$.
Scene Objects and Initial State: 2D coordinate viewport displaying car $C$ (mass $m = 1000.0\text{ kg}$) navigating a flat circular curve of radius $\rho = 100.0\text{ m}$ at speed $v = 20.0\text{ m/s}$. Curvature center point $O'$ marked with crosshair. Moving $n$-$t$ frame attached to car. Vector overlay attached to car $C$: Green normal force arrow $\sum F_n$ (supplied by tire friction $F_f$) pointing inward to center $O'$, Green normal acceleration vector arrow $a_n$ parallel to $\sum F_n$. Skid warning indicator banner (inactive). Digital readout panel: speed $v = 20.0\text{ m/s}$, curvature radius $\rho = 100.0\text{ m}$, normal acceleration $a_n = v^2/\rho = 4.0\text{ m/s}^2$, required centripetal force $\sum F_n = 4000.0\text{ N}$, available static friction limit $F_{s,max} = \mu_s mg = 4905.0\text{ N}$ (\\(\mu_s = 0.5\\)).
Time Behavior: Continuous execution or parameter slider modification updates car speed $v$, recalculating required normal force demand $m v^2/\rho$ and triggering skid warning if demand exceeds static friction limit $F_{s,max}$.
Custom Perspectives: Direction Bending Task Perspective: Demonstrating visually that normal force $\sum F_n$ performs zero work (\\(\mathbf{F}_n \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0\\)) and acts exclusively to bend the velocity vector direction toward curvature center $O'$.
Governing Rules: Normal equation of motion: $\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}$. Centripetal acceleration formula: $a_n = \frac{v^2}{\rho}$. Static friction grip limit: $F_{s,max} = \mu_s N = \mu_s mg$. Skidding threshold equation: $m \frac{v^2}{\rho} > \mu_s mg \implies v_{max} = \sqrt{\mu_s g \rho}$.
Learner Investigations and Controls:
- Car Speed Slider (\\(v\\)): Learner adjusts turning speed $v \in [0.0\text{ m/s}, 40.0\text{ m/s}]$.
- Curve Radius Slider (\\(\rho\\)): Learner adjusts track radius $\rho \in [20.0\text{ m}, 200.0\text{ m}]$.
- Static Friction Coefficient Slider (\\(\mu_s\\)): Learner adjusts tire grip $\mu_s \in [0.1, 0.9]$.
- Dynamic Force Balance Panel Toggle: Shows or hides force comparison meter ($F_{required}$ vs $F_{available}$).
- Investigation Action: Set $\rho = 100.0\text{ m}, \mu_s = 0.5$ and increase speed slider $v$ from $20.0\text{ m/s} \to 25.0\text{ m/s}$.
- Visible Consequence: At $v = 20.0\text{ m/s}$, required normal force calculates as $\sum F_n = 1000 \times \frac{20^2}{100} = 4000.0\text{ N} \le 4905.0\text{ N}$; green arrow holds car in stable circular path. Increasing speed to $v = 25.0\text{ m/s}$ increases normal acceleration demand to $a_n = \frac{25^2}{100} = 6.25\text{ m/s}^2$ and required centripetal force to $6250.0\text{ N}$; since $6250.0\text{ N} > 4905.0\text{ N}$, skid warning alarm flashes red, green force arrow snaps, and car skids radially outward off circular track.
Linked Representations: Car position on circular track, green $F_n$ arrow length, center point $O'$, skid warning banner, force comparison meter, and digital readout panel are fully synchronized.
Visual Outcome and Misconception Contrast: Proves that normal force demand grows quadratically with speed (\\(a_n \propto v^2\\)), correcting the misconception that doubling speed only doubles required turning force (doubling speed quadruples required centripetal force).
Acceptance Requirements:
1. Verify $a_n = 4.0\text{ m/s}^2$ and required force $\sum F_n = 4000.0\text{ N}$ for $m = 1000.0\text{ kg}, v = 20.0\text{ m/s}, \rho = 100.0\text{ m}$.
2. Verify maximum safe speed $v_{max} = 19.81\text{ m/s}$ (\\(71.3\text{ km/h}\\)) for $\rho = 80.0\text{ m}, \mu_s = 0.5$.
3. Verify car skids outward when required centripetal force exceeds available static friction.
Limitations: Outward centrifugal fictitious forces are omitted.

* Primary learning objective: Formulate the normal equation of motion \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\), establishing that centripetal force \\(\sum F_n\\) acts perpendicular to motion toward the center of curvature \\(O'\\), causing direction change proportional to \\(v^2\\) and inversely proportional to \\(\rho\\).
* Essential and supporting perspectives: Essential: Center-Directed Centripetal Force Perspective (identifying \\(\sum F_n\\) as the required inward physical force pulling particle into a curved trajectory), Curvature Geometry Reaction Perspective (linking \\(a_n = v^2/\rho\\) to curvature radius \\(\rho\\)). first_output.core_understanding:
* Baseline concept: Resolving Newton's Second Law along the normal axis \\(n\\) yields \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\). The normal axis \\(n\\) always points inward toward the center of curvature \\(O'\\). Therefore, normal acceleration \\(a_n = \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\) is always positive and directed toward \\(O'\\). The net normal force \\(\sum F_n\\) (centripetal force) must be supplied by physical forces such as friction \\(F_f\\), normal surface reactions \\(N\\), or cable tension \\(T\\). Without sufficient inward normal force \\(\sum F_n\\), the particle cannot maintain the curve of radius \\(\rho\\) and will slide outward to a larger radius.
* Time Perspective: Higher instantaneous speed \\(v\\) requires quadratically higher centripetal force (\\(\sum F_n \propto v^2\\)) to hold path curvature.
* Custom perspectives: Direction Bending Task Perspective: Normal force \\(\sum F_n\\) performs zero work (\\(\sum F_n \perp \mathbf{v}\\)) and acts solely to bend the velocity vector direction toward curvature center \\(O'\\).
* Perspective connections: Normal force magnitude directly limits maximum safe speed \\(v_{max} = \sqrt{\frac{\rho \sum F_{n,max}}{m}}\\) along curved paths.

Attached green normal acceleration vector arrow \\(a_n = \frac{20^2}{100} = 4.0\text{ m/s}^2\\). Digital readout panel displaying required centripetal force \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = 1000 \times 4.0 = 4000\text{ N}\\) and available static friction limit \\(F_{s,max} = \mu_s N = 0.5 \times 9810 = 4905\text{ N}\\).
* Literal vs. metaphorical: Car, curved track, center point \\(O'\\), tire friction force arrow, and normal acceleration arrow are literal physical overlays.
* Metaphor limits: Normal force arrow length increases quadratically with speed \\(v^2\\).
first_output.visual_scene_script:
* Normal explanatory sequence: Car (\\(m = 1000\text{ kg}\\)) turns radius \\(\rho = 100\text{ m}\\) at \\(v = 20\text{ m/s}\\). Required centripetal acceleration is \\(a_n = \frac{20^2}{100} = 4.0\text{ m/s}^2\\), requiring inward friction force \\(\sum F_n = 4000\text{ N}\\).
* Alternative conditions and observable outcomes: If speed increases to \\(v = 25\text{ m/s}\\), required normal acceleration jumps to \\(a_n = \frac{25^2}{100} = 6.25\text{ m/s}^2\\), requiring centripetal force \\(\sum F_n = 6250\text{ N}\\). Since required force exceeds available static friction limit (\\(4905\text{ N}\\)), tire grip fails (\\(\sum F_n < m v^2/\rho\\)), and car skids radially outward off the track.

* Specified interactions: Slide speed \\(v\\) or radius \\(\rho \to\\) Required centripetal force updates \\(\to\\) Governing rules \\(a_n = v^2/\rho\\) and \\(F_{s,max} = \mu_s mg \to\\) Green force arrow resizes; if \\(m a_n > F_{s,max}\\), car skids off track.

first_output.concept_check:
* Activity: A \\(1000\text{-kg}\\) car rounds a flat curve of radius \\(\rho = 80\text{ m}\\) on a road with static friction coefficient \\(\mu_s = 0.5\\). Calculate the maximum speed \\(v_{max}\\) the car can achieve without skidding.
* Expected observation: Maximum safe speed \\(v_{max} = \sqrt{\mu_s g \rho} = \sqrt{0.5 \times 9.81 \times 80} = \sqrt{392.4} \approx 19.81\text{ m/s}\\) (\\(71.3\text{ km/h}\\)).

first_output.conceptual_summary: * The normal equation of motion \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\) governs directional turning. Centripetal force \\(\sum F_n\\) acts toward curvature center \\(O'\\); if physical friction or normal forces cannot supply \\(m v^2/\rho\\), path stability fails.
first_output.colloquial_egyptian_explanation: * معادلة الحركة العمودية \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\) هي المسئولة عن دوران الجسم ودخوله في الملفات. القوة العمودية \\(\sum F_n\\) بتسمى قوة الجذب المركزي (Centripetal Force) وبتكون ديماً موجهة لداخل الملف ناحية مركز التقعر \\(O'\\). القوة دي غالباً بينتجها احتكاك العجل مع الأرض \\(F_f\\). ولو سرعة العربية زادت جداً، القوة المتاحة للاحتكاك مش هتكفي الاحتياج \\(m v^2/\rho\\) والعربية هتزحف لبره الملف (Skid).
first_output.laws_if_any:
* Normal equation of motion: \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\)
* Maximum non-skid speed on flat curve: \\(v_{max} = \sqrt{\mu_s g \rho}\\)
* Required centripetal force: \\(F_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\)
* Units: Force in Newtons (\\(\text{N}\\)), Radius in meters (\\(\text{m}\\)), Speed in \\(\text{m/s}\\).
first_output.real_life_example:
* لما تلف بعربيتك في ملف ضيق بسرعة عالية في يوم ممطر: المطر بيقلل معامل الاحتكاك \\(\mu_s\\)، فـ قوة الاحتكاك المتاحة بين العجل والأرض بتقل. لو دخلت الملف بنفس سرعتك العادية، قوة الاحتكاك مش هتقدر تدي العربية العجلة العمودية المطلوبة (\\(a_n = v^2/\rho\\))، وهتكتشف إن العربية بتتسحب بره الطريق غصب عنك!

perspective_map.primary_learning_objective: Formulate normal equation of motion \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\), establishing that centripetal force \\(\sum F_n\\) acts toward curvature center \\(O'\\), causing direction change proportional to \\(v^2/\rho\\).
perspective_map.baseline_objects_and_state: Car \\(C\\) (\\(m = 1000\text{ kg}\\)) on flat curve (\\(\rho = 100\text{ m}\\)), center point \\(O'\\), green inward friction force arrow \\(F_f\\), green normal acceleration arrow \\(a_n = 4.0\text{ m/s}^2\\), digital readouts for speed \\(v\\), required force \\(m a_n\\), and friction limit \\(F_{s,max}\\).
perspective_map.time_perspective: Instantaneous speed \\(v\\) determines required quadratic centripetal force demand (\\(m v^2/\rho\\)).
perspective_map.custom_perspectives: Direction Bending Task Perspective: Normal force \\(\sum F_n\\) performs zero work (\\(\sum F_n \perp \mathbf{v}\\)) and acts solely to bend velocity vector direction toward curvature center \\(O'\\).
perspective_map.governing_behavior: \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\); \\(F_{s,max} = \mu_s N = \mu_s mg\\); Skid condition: \\(m \frac{v^2}{\rho} > \mu_s mg \implies v > \sqrt{\mu_s g \rho}\\).
perspective_map.learner_investigations: Investigation: Determine skid threshold speed on flat circular curve for varying road friction. Action: slide speed \\(v \in [0, 40\text{ m/s}]\\) or friction coefficient \\(\mu_s \in [0.1, 0.9]\\). Affected state: required centripetal force \\(m v^2/\rho\\), green normal force arrow length, skid warning alarm, car path trajectory. Visible consequence: At \\(v = 20\text{ m/s}, \rho = 100\text{ m}, \mu_s = 0.5\\), required centripetal force is \\(4000\text{ N} \le F_{s,max} (4905\text{ N})\\); green arrow holds car in stable circular turn. Increasing speed to \\(v = 25\text{ m/s}\\) increases centripetal demand to \\(6250\text{ N} > 4905\text{ N}\\); skid warning flashes, green force arrow breaks, and car skids radially outward off circular track. Contrasting case: banked turn where surface angle supplies centripetal force.
perspective_map.controls: Car speed slider \\(v \in [0, 40\text{ m/s}]\\); Curve radius slider \\(\rho \in [20, 200\text{ m}]\\); Static friction slider \\(\mu_s \in [0.1, 0.9]\\); Force balance panel toggle.
perspective_map.linked_views: Car position on circular track, green \\(F_n\\) arrow, center point \\(O'\\), skid warning indicator, and dynamic force equation panel are fully synchronized.
perspective_map.visual_learning_goal: Master normal equation of motion \\(\sum F_n = m a_n = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}\\) and evaluate non-skid speed limits on flat curves.
perspective_map.coverage: Normal equation of motion \\(\sum F_n = m a_n\\), centripetal acceleration \\(a_n = v^2/\rho\\), center of curvature \\(O'\\), static friction limit, and skidding threshold mapped.
perspective_map.acceptance_checks: Verify \\(a_n = 4.0\text{ m/s}^2\\) and \\(\sum F_n = 4000\text{ N}\\) for \\(m = 1000\text{ kg}, v = 20\text{ m/s}, \rho = 100\text{ m}\\); verify \\(v_{max} = 19.81\text{ m/s}\\) for \\(\rho = 80\text{ m}, \mu_s = 0.5\\).

scenes.section_title:
* Primary learning objective: Establish binormal force equilibrium \\(\sum F_b = 0\\) (since \\(a_b = 0\\) for planar curves) and analyze banked curve mechanics (\\(\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho}\\)), determining optimum banking angles that eliminate reliance on tire friction.
* Essential and supporting perspectives: Essential: Binormal Zero-Acceleration Perspective (\\(\sum F_b = m a_b = 0\\) confirming motion is confined to osculating plane), Banked Normal Component Tilt Perspective (resolving normal surface reaction \\(N\\) to provide both vertical weight support \\(N\cos\theta = mg\\) and centripetal turning force \\(N\sin\theta = m v^2/\rho\\)). Supporting: Highway Engineering Design Perspective.
* Important evidence gaps: Aerodynamic downforce and vehicle roll suspension compliance are omitted.
scenes.generated_prompt:
Scene Type: Process
Learning Target: Establish binormal force equilibrium $\sum F_b = 0$ and analyze banked curve mechanics (\\(\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho}\\)), evaluating vehicle turning stability without relying on friction.
Scene Objects and Initial State: 2D cross-sectional viewport displaying highway banked curve angled at $\theta = 20.0^\circ$ to horizontal. Car model $C$ (mass $m = 1200.0\text{ kg}$) rounding curve of radius $\rho = 200.0\text{ m}$ at rated speed $v = 26.7\text{ m/s}$ (\\(96.0\text{ km/h}\\)). Free-Body Diagram overlay on car cross-section: Weight vector $W = mg = 11772.0\text{ N}$ (pointing vertically downward), Normal reaction vector $N = \frac{mg}{\cos 20^\circ} = 12528.0\text{ N}$ (tilted $20.0^\circ$ inward from vertical). Component triangle overlay: Vertical normal component $N\cos 20^\circ = 11772.0\text{ N}$ (balancing weight $W$), Horizontal normal component $N\sin 20^\circ = 4285.0\text{ N}$ (pointing horizontally toward curvature center). Digital readout panel: bank angle $\theta = 20.0^\circ$, radius $\rho = 200.0\text{ m}$, rated speed $v_{rated} = \sqrt{g\rho \tan\theta} = 26.7\text{ m/s}$, required centripetal force $m v^2/\rho = 4285.0\text{ N}$, live formulas $N\cos\theta = mg$, $N\sin\theta = m v^2/\rho$, $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho}$.
Time Behavior: Continuous execution or parameter modification recalculates force components, updating tilted normal vector $N$ and highlighting lateral force balance along road surface.
Custom Perspectives: Ideal No-Friction Rated Speed Perspective: Demonstrating visually that banked road angles utilize surface geometry to tilt normal reaction $N$, providing required centripetal force $N\sin\theta = m v^2/\rho$ to secure vehicle turning stability at rated speed without relying on tire friction.
Governing Rules: Binormal equilibrium: $\sum F_b = N\cos\theta - mg = 0 \implies N = \frac{mg}{\cos\theta}$. Horizontal normal equation: $\sum F_n = N\sin\theta = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}$. Ideal banking angle formula: $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho}$. Rated no-friction speed formula: $v_{rated} = \sqrt{g\rho \tan\theta}$.
Learner Investigations and Controls:
- Bank Angle Slider (\\(\theta\\)): Learner adjusts road incline angle $\theta \in [0.0^\circ, 45.0^\circ]$.
- Car Speed Slider (\\(v\\)): Learner adjusts vehicle speed $v \in [0.0\text{ m/s}, 50.0\text{ m/s}]$.
- Friction Coefficient Slider (\\(\mu_s\\)): Learner sets road surface friction $\mu_s \in [0.0, 0.8]$.
- Force Component Triangle Toggle: Shows or hides scalar vector decomposition triangle (\\(N\cos\theta, N\sin\theta, W\\)).
- Investigation Action: Set $\rho = 200.0\text{ m}, \theta = 20.0^\circ, \mu_s = 0.0$ (icy surface) and adjust speed slider $v$ below and above rated speed $26.7\text{ m/s}$.
- Visible Consequence: At $v = 26.7\text{ m/s}$, horizontal normal force component $N\sin 20^\circ = 4285.0\text{ N}$ matches required centripetal force $m v^2/\rho = 4285.0\text{ N}$ exactly; car remains perfectly centered in lane without friction. Reducing speed to $v = 15.0\text{ m/s}$ drops required centripetal force to $1350.0\text{ N}$; excess inward normal component forces car to slide down the icy incline. Increasing speed to $v = 35.0\text{ m/s}$ increases required centripetal force to $7350.0\text{ N}$; insufficient inward component forces car to slide up the banked ramp.
Linked Representations: Car cross-section on banked ramp, tilted normal vector $N$, weight vector $W$, horizontal centripetal component $N\sin\theta$, lateral incline slip arrow, and digital readout panel are fully synchronized.
Visual Outcome and Misconception Contrast: Proves that banked angles allow vehicles to turn safely at rated speeds without friction (\\(\tan\theta = v^2/g\rho\\)), correcting the misconception that turning always requires tire friction on flat road surfaces.
Acceptance Requirements:
1. Verify ideal banking angle $\theta = 20.0^\circ$ for $v = 26.7\text{ m/s}$ (\\(96.0\text{ km/h}\\)), $\rho = 200.0\text{ m}$.
2. Verify ideal banking angle $\theta = 31.48^\circ$ for $v = 30.0\text{ m/s}$ (\\(108.0\text{ km/h}\\)), $\rho = 150.0\text{ m}$.
3. Verify horizontal normal component $N\sin\theta$ equals $m v^2/\rho$ at rated speed.
Limitations: Aerodynamic downforce and vehicle suspension roll effects are omitted.

first_output.section_identity:
* Primary learning objective: Establish binormal force equilibrium \\(\sum F_b = 0\\) (since \\(a_b = 0\\) for planar curves) and analyze banked curve mechanics (\\(\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho}\\)), determining optimum banking angles that eliminate reliance on tire friction.
* Essential and supporting perspectives: Essential: Binormal Zero-Acceleration Perspective (\\(\sum F_b = m a_b = 0\\) confirming motion is confined to osculating plane), Banked Normal Component Tilt Perspective (resolving normal surface reaction \\(N\\) to provide both vertical weight support \\(N\cos\theta = mg\\) and centripetal turning force \\(N\sin\theta = m v^2/\rho\\)). Supporting: Highway Engineering Design Perspective.
* Important evidence gaps: Aerodynamic downforce and vehicle roll suspension compliance are omitted.
first_output.core_understanding:
* Baseline concept: The binormal axis \\(b\\) is perpendicular to both tangential axis \\(t\\) and normal axis \\(n\\) (\\(\mathbf{u}_b = \mathbf{u}_t \times \mathbf{u}_n\\)). Because motion is confined to the osculating plane, there is no displacement or acceleration along \\(b\\), yielding binormal equilibrium: \\(\sum F_b = 0\\). On a banked roadway angled at \\(\theta\\) to the horizontal, the normal surface reaction \\(N\\) tilts inward. Resolving forces yields:
Vertical equilibrium: $\sum F_z = N \cos\theta - mg = 0 \implies N \cos\theta = mg$.
Horizontal normal motion: $\sum F_n = N \sin\theta = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}$.
Dividing the two equations gives the ideal banking angle equation: $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho}$. At this rated speed $v = \sqrt{g\rho \tan\theta}$, a vehicle navigates the curve safely even on zero-friction ice without slipping.
* Time Perspective: Banked curves provide passive, speed-dependent centripetal acceleration independent of friction degradation over time.
* Custom perspectives: Ideal No-Friction Rated Speed Perspective: Banked angles replace precarious tire friction with structural surface geometry to provide required centripetal force.
* Perspective connections: Combining vertical equilibrium (\\(\sum F_b = 0\\)) and radial centripetal force (\\(\sum F_n = m a_n\\)) determines optimal civil engineering highway geometry.

Car \\(C\\) (\\(m = 1200\text{ kg}\\)) moving at rated speed \\(v = 26.7\text{ m/s}\\) (\\(96\text{ km/h}\\)) around radius \\(\rho = 200\text{ m}\\). Free-Body Diagram overlaid: Weight \\(W = mg = 11772\text{ N}\\) (downward), Normal force \\(N\\) tilted inward at \\(20^\circ\\) to vertical. Component triangle showing horizontal normal force component \\(N\sin 20^\circ = 4285\text{ N}\\) supplying exact centripetal force \\(m v^2/\rho = 1200 \times \frac{26.7^2}{200} = 4285\text{ N}\\).
* Literal vs. metaphorical: Banked road surface, car cross-section, weight arrow, and tilted normal force arrow are literal physical overlays.
* Metaphor limits: Ideal banking angle formula assumes zero lateral friction force along road incline.
first_output.visual_scene_script:
* Normal explanatory sequence: Highway turn radius \\(\rho = 200\text{ m}\\) designed for rated speed \\(v = 26.7\text{ m/s}\\) (\\(96\text{ km/h}\\)). Ideal banking angle calculates as \\(\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho} = \frac{26.7^2}{9.81 \times 200} = \frac{712.9}{1962} = 0.3633 \implies \theta = 20.0^\circ\\).
* Alternative conditions and observable outcomes: If car travels on icy road (\\(\mu_s = 0\\)) at exact rated speed \\(26.7\text{ m/s}\\), horizontal normal component \\(N\sin 20^\circ\\) supplies \\(100\%\\) of required centripetal force, and car stays perfectly centered without sliding up or down the ramp. If car speeds up to \\(v = 35\text{ m/s}\\), required centripetal force rises, forcing car to rely on friction or slide up the banked ramp.
* Learner intervention points: Learner adjusts bank angle slider \\(\theta\\), speed slider \\(v\\), and friction coefficient \\(\mu_s\\), observing lateral force balance along road incline.

* Specified interactions: Adjust bank angle slider \\(\theta\\) or speed slider \\(v \to\\) Force components update \\(\to\\) Governing rules \\(N\cos\theta = mg\\) and \\(N\sin\theta = m v^2/\rho \to\\) Normal force vector tilts and rated speed readout recalculates.
* Control distinction: Bank angle slider alters road geometry; speed slider alters dynamic turning demand.
first_output.visual_learning_outcome: * Main outcome: Learner evaluates binormal equilibrium (\\(\sum F_b = 0\\)) and calculates ideal banking angles (\\(\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho}\\)) and non-skid speed limits for banked highway curves.
first_output.concept_check:
* Activity: Determine the ideal banking angle \\(\theta\\) for a racetrack turn of radius \\(\rho = 150\text{ m}\\) designed for cars traveling at \\(v = 30\text{ m/s}\\) (\\(\approx 108\text{ km/h}\\)) without relying on friction.
* Expected observation: Banking angle \\(\theta = 31.48^\circ\\).
* Explanation: \\(\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho} = \frac{30^2}{9.81 \times 150} = \frac{900}{1471.5} = 0.6116 \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.6116) = 31.48^\circ\\).
first_output.conceptual_summary: * Binormal force equilibrium (\\(\sum F_b = 0\\)) reflects zero out-of-plane acceleration. Banked curves tilt normal reaction \\(N\\), providing inward centripetal force \\(N\sin\theta = m v^2/\rho\\) to secure vehicle turning stability at rated speed \\(v = \sqrt{g\rho \tan\theta}\\) without friction.
first_output.colloquial_egyptian_explanation:
* المحور الثالث في المحاور المماسية والعمودية هو المحور العمودي المزدوج \\(b\\) (Binormal axis). وبما إن حركة الجسم محصورة في مستوى المنحنى، مفيش أي تسارع في اتجاه \\(b\\) وبالتالي الاتزان تام: \\(\sum F_b = 0\\).
تطبيق جميل جداً على ده هو الطرق المائلة في الملفات (Banked Curves): لما بنميل الطريق بزاوية $\theta$، رد فعل الأرض $N$ بيميل لجوه، وبيتحلل لمركبتين:
1) رأسية بتوازن الوزن: $N \cos\theta = mg$.
2) أفقية بتدينا قوة الجذب المركزي للدوران من غير ما نحتاج احتكاك خالص: $N \sin\theta = m \frac{v^2}{\rho}$.
بقسمة المعادلتين على بعض بنطلع بقانون زاوية ميل الطريق المثالية: $\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho}$.
first_output.laws_if_any:
* Binormal equilibrium: \\(\sum F_b = 0\\)
* Ideal banking angle (no friction): \\(\tan\theta = \frac{v^2}{g\rho}\\)
* Rated no-friction speed: \\(v_{rated} = \sqrt{g\rho \tan\theta}\\)
* Banked curve with friction bounds: \\(\tan(\theta \mp \phi_s) \le \frac{v^2}{g\rho} \le \tan(\theta + \phi_s)\\) where \\(\phi_s = \tan^{-1}\mu_s\\).
* Units: Angle \\(\theta\\) in degrees (\\(\text{deg}\\)) or radians, Speed in \\(\text{m/s}\\), Radius in \\(\text{m}\\).
first_output.real_life_example: * حلبة سباقات السيارات (NASCAR) أو مدارات الدراجات الهوائية (Velodrome): المنحنيات هناك بتكون مائلة بدرجة كبيرة جداً تصل لـ \\(30^\circ\\) أو أكثر. الميل العالي ده بيسمح للعربيات والدراجات إنها تلف بسرعة هائلة جداً بفضل المركبة الأفقية لرد فعل الأرض المائلة \\(N\sin\theta\\)، من غير ما تعتمد على احتكاك الكاوتش، وبدون ما تزحف لبره السباق!
